lecons.html:
Praying is a command of God. It is not simply a human necessity, a principle of spiritual connection, or a means of obtaining things we cannot obtain humanly. It is an order coming directly from God (Jer 33:3; Phil 4:6-7).

Reading the previous verses shows that not only is praying an order from God, but it has a reason. God did not command us to pray for his own whims. God wants us to pray so that he may give us the things we need or grant us revelations necessary for our life and ministry.

Normally God has the right and the power to give or reveal things to us without our praying. He has full knowledge of everything we need, so there is no necessity to inform him of anything. But he insists that we pray. The reason is the law of delegation.

The Bible says: The heavens are Yahweh’s heavens, but he has given the earth to the children of men. (Ps 115:16) This does not mean that the heavens belong to God and the earth to men. On the contrary: Behold, to Yahweh your God belongs heaven, the heaven of heavens, and the earth, with all that is therein. (Deut 10:14) The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it. (Ps 24:1) The earth belongs to God just as the heavens do. But he gave it to humanity. When God created man, he gave him dominion over all the earth and everything related to it: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them. God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.” (Gen 1:27-28) So from the beginning God delegated to man the administration of affairs related to the earth. Man sold his rights to Satan by his disobedience to God in favor of the devil’s word. Jesus Christ took this authority back for us by redeeming us with his blood.

This delegation of power is the reason why prayer is indispensable: it is at the moment of prayer that we open ourselves to communion with God. It is through prayer that we give heaven, in a way, the authorization to act on earth. That is to say, if God acted on earth without prayer being presented as the reason, he would be violating the rule of delegation. God certainly has the right to do so since everything belongs to him, but he respects principles. God does not argue with us over what he has given us. For God does not repent of his gifts and his calling (Rom 11:29).

An example in the Bible is God’s movement before the destruction of Sodom. God having found in Abraham someone who by faith is eligible to occupy the post that Adam deserted, tells himself that he cannot act without informing him. He even obtained the right to inform him by presenting himself as a passerby well received by Abraham. Then God tells him that he wants to destroy Sodom and explains that it is because people have cried out against the city to God. So God came down to act because people cried out. Then God waits to see what Abraham will do about it. And in the end God will save Lot by listening to Abraham’s (unexpressed) cry of the heart. So we can say that on earth God does nothing unless it is to answer prayers.

Why does God answer prayers? God did not hand the earth over to man’s power so that chaos would reign there. God wants the earth to be a good place to live. So he takes advantage of the contact allowed by man to fill him with his presence and with the resources of good governance and good stewardship. This contact is prayer. And when man needs supernatural, that is, superhuman, interventions, God makes them available by answering his prayer. Since sin entered the world, there is much suffering on this earth and God’s heart is grieved. But his hands remain tied as long as no one prays. So, as soon as someone prays, God seizes the opportunity. No prayer forces God. It should rather be said that it is God who leads us to pray by his Spirit in order to reach his objectives on earth.

But then what about prayers that remain unanswered? No prayer is neglected before God. But some are not taken into account by divine action because they do not line up with God’s will. Other prayers correspond to what God would do later and so must wait. Still others are prayers whose answer depends on certain conditions. For example, when one asks for the death of an enemy in the imprecatory prayer, God will certainly kill the wicked. But it will be after offering him the grace to be saved. And this repeatedly. If the wicked accepts this grace, he is saved and will not die. If he rejects this grace, he will die. But the time of grace can be very long. That is why we must never base our happiness on what is going to happen to someone else, whether good or bad.

Prayers that go in the direction of people’s well-being and salvation are more likely to be answered. Prayers that ask for inner transformation for oneself are more likely to be answered. Prayers that ask for the revelation and direction of the Holy Spirit are more likely to be answered. God will not give us what he does not want to give us even if we shout at him. So we must study and meditate on the Word of God to know his will and pray in line with it.

Pray for the cause of Christ in you and around you; and you will be answered without fail. This is what is called praying in the name of Jesus Christ. It is he who says: Until now, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be made full. (John 16:24) We must settle everything by prayer. What is not settled in prayer will remain forever without a solution despite appearances.

To pray is to worship, to address requests, supplications, and thanksgivings to God the Father, and to fight in his company for his kingdom, by the Holy Spirit, in the name of Jesus Christ.

Following the definition we have the following elements, which should not be called steps since they intertwine.

  • Come to God with confidence. He is your Father. Manners and positions do not matter. You must present yourself with love and reverence. Do whatever you want for your father; it is he.
  • Speak by the Holy Spirit: Go gently, do not rush to speak. You can remain silent, you can also speak in tongues.
  • Ask in the name of Jesus Christ. Ask as if it were Jesus Christ doing it, because it really is him. You are members of the body of Christ. Each of the members represents him. When you get on your knees, it is Christ who does it. Go all the way, do not hold back.
  • Listen: You must not be the only one to speak. God has his say. It is in fact there that the answer to your prayer begins. To listen well, it is fitting to read the Bible and meditate on it in calm.

What do we do when we pray, or what should we do?

Repentance

(Ps 66:18; 1 John 1:9; Ps 32:5; Prov 28:13)

  • Confession: Confess your sins to God, tell God concretely what you did wrong and accept his forgiveness.

Serving the Lord (ministering to him)

(Acts 13:1)

  • Praise and Worship (Ps 22:3; Eph 5:19; Col 3:16; Ps 29:2; Ps 99:5, 9; Ps 96; John 4:23-24)
  • Thanksgiving (Eph 5:20; Col 1:12; 1 Thess 5:18)
  • Proclaiming God’s mighty deeds (Ps 145:21; Ps 150:2)

Presenting one’s needs

  • Prayer of faith: Asking according to the Scriptures (1 John 5:14-15; Mark 11:23-24)
  • Supplication: Asking for things the Bible does not directly offer. (Example: asking for a particular gift of the Holy Spirit, a motorbike, a car, a house…) (Phil 4:6)

Consecration

  • Humbling oneself before God: Submitting to God’s will (Matt 26:39; John 6:38)

Fighting

  • Taking up God’s weapons (Eph 6:10-18)
  • Imposing God’s will (Matt 6:10; Acts 21:14; Col 4:12)
  • Foiling the enemy’s plans (Rom 15:30-31)
  • Clearing the way for the gospel (Eph 6:19; Phil 1:27; Col 4:3; 2 Thess 3:1)
  • Strengthening God’s ministers (Heb 13:18-19)
  • Strengthening the saints (Col 4:12)

Interceding

  • The salvation of souls (1 Tim 2:1)
  • Forgiveness and restoration of the saints (Ezek 22:30)
  • The nation (Jer 29:7)
  • The Church: missionaries, workers, new converts (Eph 6:18)

Working in the spirit (giving birth to something according to God’s will)

  • Prayer in tongues (1 Cor 14:4, 14-15)
  • Interpreting (if possible) (1 Cor 14:13)
  • Prophesying (Blessing, possessing, sealing, according to the word and instructions of the Holy Spirit) (Num 6:24-27)

Spending time with the Lord

  • Waiting at one’s post (Hab 2:1)
  • Listening (Ps 85:8, Isa 50:4)
  • Contemplating (Ps 5:3, 63:2, 119:18)

lecons.titre: The different types of prayer in the Bible
lecons.html:
1. The prayer of worship

Very few people practice it, yet it is the most powerful of all prayers. This type of prayer is focused on worshiping the Lord out of deep love, respect and admiration. These prayers come from a sincere reverence for who God is and for everything he does. It is a recommendation for everything that exists on earth (Ps 148:7-13, Ps 150:6). This is what the elders of the Church of Antioch did regularly (Acts 13:1-2). The apostle Paul recommends it greatly (Eph 5:19, Col 3:16).

2. The prayer of thanksgiving

Prayers of thanksgiving are generally prompted by an answered prayer, a deliverance, the recognition that God is good and merciful, or simply because we have received another day of life. It is also a prayer that must be joined to a supplication as Phil 4:6 says. The goal is to show that we believe we have been graciously received by God because of his goodness.

3. The prayer of confession

Confessing our sins is a meaningful way of praying as disciples of Jesus Christ and of obtaining forgiveness. The one who recognizes his weaknesses expresses his desire to be more in the image of God. Often, Jesus called those he interacted with to confess their sins and to sin no more. It is not about asking forgiveness for everything and nothing. It is recognizing one’s failings concretely before God and accepting forgiveness in Jesus Christ.

If you feel accused of having committed a sin, examine your life over the day or week, ask the Holy Spirit to show you your fault. If there is nothing, reject these accusations, which are only diabolical impressions aimed at stealing your joy and peace in Christ. If you discover a concrete failing, confess it and accept God’s forgiveness (Ps 32:5; 1 John 1:9). If people are affected by these faults, go and set things right with them, humbling yourself sufficiently.

4. The prayer of faith

This type of prayer rests on the intimate knowledge and trust we have in God, who made clear promises in his Word. We must believe without doubting that God is able to do what he said. This prayer consists of bringing to God what he said and telling him that we expect it without fail. As we have the same spirit of faith that is expressed in this word of Scripture: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believed, and therefore I spoke.” We also believe, and therefore we also speak; (2 Cor 4:13) Examples of things to ask for through the prayer of faith are: wisdom for victory in trials (James 1:5), healing (James 5:15), the fruit of the womb (Ps 127:3), the baptism in the Holy Spirit (Luke 11:9-13), spiritual direction (John 10:27), deliverance from the works of the wicked (2 Tim 4:18, 2 Thess 3:1-3), etc.

5. The prayer of supplication

This is the most popular and the most practiced. Here we lay before God our concerns, our desires, our expectations, our wishes. These are things that are not clearly covered by biblical promises (Phil 4:6). When we make this kind of prayer, the answer is immediate. But it is not what we often think. We too often expect miracles that bring us into possession of the things we asked for. That is not it. The answer to every prayer of supplication is the action of the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, on our heart and our thoughts to keep us in Jesus Christ. This peace delivers us from the panic that can lead us to fall into more trouble while looking for a solution to what we already have as a challenge. Moreover, this peace lets us think calmly in order to enter the doors that God has already opened for us. That is why this prayer must always be followed by thanksgiving as a demonstration of your faith in the answer.

NB: We often make the mistake of asking for things like a motorbike, a car, a house… through the prayer of faith. Jesus said that God will give us food and clothing. He did not say a house, etc. He himself never made this request expressly. No apostle did. If we want to ask for these things, we must make them supplications. These are the desires of our hearts that we will obtain only when our hearts have found their pleasure entirely in the Lord (Ps 37:3-5).

6. The prayer of intercession

Praying for others is crucial for all who are part of the body of Christ. The Bible instructs us to pray for one another. There are a multitude of examples of intercessory prayers in the Bible. Jesus prayed not only for himself but for the disciples and for all believers in his last hours before being arrested (John 17). The apostle Paul wrote that he often kept other Christians in his prayers (Col 1:9-11). Intercession is truly required for healing, because the sick person is often weakened and overwhelmed by pessimistic thoughts. Other people are needed to have faith for him. Jesus healed the paralytic because of the faith of his friends (Mark 2:3-11). James, who understood the mystery, tells us: Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective. (James 5:16)

7. The prayer of agreement

There is a supernatural power when several people raise their voices on the same subject. Heaven cannot resist them (Matt 18:19). For the agreement to be true, you must take the time to agree on what you want and the way you hope for it. If one person expects the sick person to get up instantly while the other only wants to pray and wait for things to happen with time, they are not in agreement.

8. The prayer of the Spirit

When we no longer have the strength to pray, when we do not know how to pray, the Holy Spirit intercedes for us with inexpressible sighs. It is not only about prayers in tongues. It can be groanings, moanings and weeping that the person praying does not control (Rom 8:26-27).

9. Prayer in the spirit

This is speaking in tongues practiced to present to God burdens that one does not master. According to the apostle Paul, when someone prays or gives thanks in the spirit, what he says is not understood by those around him. Only God understands it (1 Cor 14:2, 14, 16). In other words, he speaks in tongues. One can do it alone or in a group. It is a prayer that addresses God directly, bypassing human thought, whether that of the one praying or of those who hear. It is a prayer that builds up the one who prays but also leaves room for the Holy Spirit to act beyond our knowledge. All the other kinds of prayer can be made by means of prayer in tongues. One can intercede, petition, give thanks, worship, make imprecations, etc. It is not necessary to interpret prayer in tongues unless you do it alone in the presence of people who need to hear what you say. That said, interpreting your own prayer in tongues offers even more benefits. So it is fitting to ask for the gift of interpretation. Many people argue against prayer in the spirit using the words of the apostle Paul. We must face the fact that he was correcting abuses. He was not rising up against this grace as many do today. Before looking at the apostle’s negations in his chapters, we must first know his teaching by looking at the positive aspects of his letter: “For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God … but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries. He who speaks in another language edifies himself … For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays … I will pray with the spirit … I will sing with the spirit … you most certainly give thanks well … I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.” (1 Cor 14:2, 4, 14-18). We must pray in tongues. And we must do it a lot!

10. The prayer of blessing

Prayers of blessing are words of blessing that we generally proclaim over a person or sometimes over ourselves. They are often said when we enter a new season of our life. We pray blessings over newlyweds, newborns, or even over a new house, a new job/position or a car for example. Prayers of blessing are found throughout Scripture and are powerful means of asking that the best of God be poured out (Phil 1:9-11).

11. The prayer of imprecation

These are used to call down God’s judgment on the wicked and thus avenge the righteous. They are found a lot in the Psalms. As for me, I will call on God. Yahweh will save me. (Ps 55:16) It is a prayer that appeals to God’s justice and asks for vengeance. This type of prayer is controversial today because Jesus teaches us to pray that our enemies be blessed, not cursed (Matt 5:44-48). The apostle Paul says expressly: “Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don’t curse.” (Rom 12:14). In view of this, one can be completely against the prayer of imprecations. Only Jesus Christ did not spare his words when he had to express God’s judgment against the son of perdition and all who cause God’s children to stumble: “For the Son of Man goes, even as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.” (Mark 14:21). “He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come! It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.” (Luke 17:1-2). When we pray we must not hesitate to pronounce God’s judgment against the wicked, mainly those who act by mystical powers and are out of reach of our intervention of kindness. If we are led by the love of God, we can trust the Holy Spirit as we pray.

That said, do not fight anyone directly. Despite all the knowledge you may have, despite everything you may know about someone, who he is, the practices he has, the religion he follows, the powers attributed to him, the dangerousness of his powers and practices, do not fight him. If you know with certainty that some of his practices are weapons directed against you, destroy their effect by confessing the word of God: No weapon that is formed against you will prevail; and you will condemn every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of Yahweh’s servants, and their righteousness is of me,” says Yahweh. (Isa 54:17) Above all avoid taking the person as an enemy and directing your prayer against him. Do not let him possess your thoughts. Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good. (Rom 12:21) Keep your faith in God’s faithfulness. He promised to be with you and to fight for you. Let him do it: Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh, which he will work for you today; for you will never again see the Egyptians whom you have seen today. Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.” (Exod 14:13-14)

To keep praying, you need determination and perseverance. Everyone has difficulty keeping a habit of prayer. We tend to neglect it. There are several reasons for this.

Prayer is spiritual exercise. All exercise is activity that requires spending energy. Physical exercise is of little profit. But we do it regularly. Spiritual exercise is profitable for everything, having benefit for this life and the one to come. So we must take it seriously. If we think of prayer as something to do when we have the right feeling, the prayer life will decline.

For every activity, you need a schedule. For prayer too, you need a dedicated moment, a duration to respect, and you must be focused. The minimum time a Christian should devote to prayer is not specified in the Bible. It says rather to pray without ceasing. That means staying constantly connected with Heaven. But we must also set aside personally planned moments for prayer, as our Lord Jesus Christ also had the habit of doing. We advise spending two hours a day in prayer. It is good to spread this time over the day, at least 1 hour in the morning and 1 hour in the evening. You must arrange the wood morning and evening so that the fire keeps burning on the altar.

Prayer is also a fight. It is hard. You must decide and discipline yourself to do it. You must watch out for the following things, which can also weaken the prayer life.

The first is the feeling that everything is fine. Definitely, a child of God cannot be perpetually under persecution or trials. There will certainly be moments of calm, rest and perfect well-being. But that is no reason to stop praying. Obviously there is no need to express before God. But you must pray. And in these moments, the prayer of thanksgiving, the prayer of worship and prayer in the spirit must be the order of the day. You must concentrate on always doing your dedicated time in prayer, and even more.

Physical fatigue can also be an obstacle to prayer. When you are tired, every task becomes boring, especially prayer. That is why you must put your prayer hours at times when you are less tired. You must also avoid overloading yourself with activities. If you see that you are overloaded with many things that you humanly have no way of getting rid of, pray and ask God to help you free yourself from what is not important even though it presents itself as such. When you have prayed, trust God and take a moment to study your commitments and activities in order to prioritize and even get rid of what serves no purpose. Also find a prayer partner and set prayer hours together. Each one must be rigorous with these hours and help his neighbor.

Another obstacle to prayer is weakness due to the state of health. If your health declines, your motivation for prayer will decrease. So you must look after your health by eating well, exercising regularly and getting adequate rest. If your health declines, even slightly, if you feel your desire to pray diminishing in you, inform your prayer partner. The Bible even says to call the elders of the church (more experienced people) to pray the prayer of faith and anoint him with oil (James 5:14-15).

Another thing that discourages and weakens the flame of prayer is the impression that the answer is delayed. Our Lord encourages us to persevere. He says: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them? I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?” (Luke 18:7-8) The faith the Lord asks for is trust in God to keep praying even when the answer seems delayed.

You must pray when things are not going well. You must keep praying when you are in joy by singing hymns. You must get help in prayer when you are physically weakened. You must keep the faith that you will definitely be answered. If God answered Elijah, he will answer us. It is good to meditate here on the words of James: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises. Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord, and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven. Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective. Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months. He prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit. (James 5:13-18)

This is a somewhat unusual prayer exercise that we encourage Christians to do at least at the beginning of each week. The verse from which this spiritual exercise is inspired does not specifically say to do this. But as we know that we can confess all parts of the Scriptures over ourselves and be transformed by it, we believe this is by no means a slip, but rather an act of faith. Moreover, it is not a doctrine. No one is saved by doing it and no one will be lost by opposing it. We only know that those who practice it obtain great spiritual benefits from it. Ralph Mahoney also recommended it in his book titled The Shepherd’s Staff.

The Builder is required to do it at least once a week

Take the Bible and read: Eph 6:10-17

Proclaim:

I strengthen myself in the Lord and in the strength of his might. I put on the whole armor of God, so that I can stand against the wiles of the devil. For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places. Therefore I take up the whole armor of God, so that I can withstand in the evil day, and, having done all, stand firm.

(Put your hands on your waist as if putting on a belt and say:) I put on the belt of truth, which is the word of God. I am the temple of the Holy Spirit. I glorify God in my spirit and my body, which belong to God (1 Cor 6:19-20). My old man was crucified with Christ, the body of sin is destroyed and I am no longer a slave to sin. It will not reign in my body and I will not obey its lusts. My sexual instinct is under the control of the Holy Spirit. God wants my sanctification, and by the Holy Spirit he sanctifies me. By his strength, I abstain from sexual immorality. I possess my body in holiness and honor. I will not give myself to passionate lust, like the pagans who do not know God. I am holy, sanctified by the Word of God.

(Put your hands on your chest:) I wear the breastplate of righteousness. In Christ, I am justified. I am the righteousness of God. I am born of God and I practice righteousness. Doing what is right is not hard for me. It is natural for me to practice righteousness because the seed of God in me is operational. And I have no difficulty sharing my resources with my brothers and sisters in the faith, following the rule of equality. Besides, I will extend a helping hand to a brother or sister this week. My emotions are controlled by the power of the Holy Spirit.

(Touch your feet as if putting on shoes and say:) I put on my spiritual shoes, the readiness of the gospel of peace. “For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.” (Rom 1:16) I am a witness of Christ and my testimony will not weaken. The Holy Spirit in me bears witness of Christ and I bear witness too. Today, I will speak of Christ to someone.

(Raise your left hand, as if holding up a shield:) I take the shield of faith. I stay founded on God’s faithfulness: All is well. Every situation is under control. I fear nothing, God is with me, he provides for my needs. He heals me, he protects me. I am under the shelter of the Most High, resting in the shadow of the Almighty. With my God I have control of the situation and I find the solution.

(Put your right hand on your head and declare:) I put on the helmet of salvation. I am saved by faith in Jesus Christ, I am a child of God. I am holy. My life is governed by the will of God, and not by the lusts of the world. I am a prince, a son of the Almighty, the holy God. I do not lower myself to live in the mire. I am a lit lamp, I stay on the lampstand and I light the world. My head is sanctified. I have the wisdom of Christ. Negative thoughts will not find fertile ground in my mind. I do not waste my time on negative thoughts. This is what finds fertile ground in my thought: everything that is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, commendable, virtuous and praiseworthy.

(Raise your right hand as if holding a sword) I have the sword of the spirit, which is the word. God has put his word in my mouth. It is living and active. At all times and in all places I will have the words needed to answer each person. No dishonest word, no deceit and no jesting comes out of my mouth. The word that comes out of my mouth gives grace to those who hear it and changes circumstances and situations for the glory of God.

objectifs: You understand why God requires prayer — the law of delegation.
You use the 11 types of prayer according to the situations of your life.
You overcome the 4 obstacles to prayer with concrete strategies.
You take up the spiritual weapons at least once a week.

qcm.q: What does the manual say about prayer?
c: It is a command of God, not only a means of obtaining what we cannot have humanly
It is an option for pastors
It is a mere human necessity

qcm.q: Why does God insist that we pray, although he knows all our needs?
c: Because he can do nothing without us
Because of the law of delegation: he gave the earth to the sons of men, and it is through prayer that we give heaven the authorization to act
qcm.e: Psalm 115:16. God respects the principles he has set.

qcm.q: Who took back for us the authority that man sold to Satan by his disobedience?
c: Jesus Christ, by redeeming us with his blood
qcm.e: See the lesson on the definition and necessity of prayer.

qcm.q: What are the elements for praying, according to the manual?
c: Praying alone, late, for a long time, in silence
Kneeling, closing your eyes, speaking loudly, fasting
Coming to God with confidence, speaking by the Holy Spirit, asking in the name of Jesus Christ, listening
qcm.e: These elements intertwine: they are not called steps.

qcm.q: What does “asking in the name of Jesus Christ” mean, according to the module?
c: Asking as if it were Jesus Christ himself doing it, because we are members of his body
Ending every prayer with the words “in Jesus’ name”
qcm.e: Each of the members of the body of Christ represents him: “go all the way, do not hold back”.

qcm.q: What is the most powerful prayer, and yet the least practiced?
qcm.e: Focused on who God is and not on requests (Acts 13:1-2).

qcm.q: What should the prayer of confession be, according to the module?
c: Telling your sins in front of the whole assembly
Asking forgiveness for everything and nothing
Recognizing your failings concretely before God and accepting his forgiveness in Jesus Christ
qcm.e: If you feel accused of a sin, examine your life and ask the Holy Spirit to show you what to confess.

qcm.q: What does the prayer of faith consist of?
c: Asking according to the Scriptures, bringing to God what he said in his Word

qcm.q: What does Matthew 18:19 say about the prayer of agreement?
c: When several agree on the same subject, it is a supernatural power

qcm.q: Why is intercession truly required for healing?
c: Because the sick person never has faith
Because the sick person is often weakened and overwhelmed by pessimistic thoughts
Because God listens only to group prayers
qcm.e: Other people are needed to pray with faith for him. Jesus prayed for his disciples and for all believers (John 17).

qcm.q: What does the Holy Spirit do in the prayer of the Spirit (Romans 8:26-27)?
c: When we no longer have strength, he intercedes for us with sighs, groanings, tears
qcm.e: This is the prayer of the Spirit, to be distinguished from prayer in the spirit (in tongues).

qcm.q: What should you do when “everything is fine” and you have no need to express?
c: Stop praying until the next need
Keep your dedicated time with worship, thanksgiving and prayer in the spirit
qcm.e: This feeling is the first obstacle to prayer.

qcm.q: What should you do against physical fatigue, an obstacle to prayer?
c: Put your prayer hours at times when you are less tired, avoid overloading yourself and find a prayer partner
qcm.e: Each one must be rigorous with the set hours and help his neighbor.

qcm.q: How much daily prayer time does the manual advise?
c: Two hours a day, spread over at least 1 hour in the morning and 1 hour in the evening
qcm.e: You must arrange the wood morning and evening so that the fire keeps burning on the altar.
